newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court rejects Commission's appeal against railway union.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects Commission's appeal against railway union.

text.p: The European Court of Justice confirmed on Tuesday that the European Commission breached procedure when it tried to fine the International Union of Railways (UIC) for competition violation.

In June, 1995 the Court of First Instance told the Commission it consulted the wrong experts to make a determination that the UIC, in distributing leaflets on railway-travel agency relationships, had violated Community rules on competition.

The Commission sought to fine the UIC one million Ecus, claiming the the UIC violated article 85(1) of the EC Treaty by setting standard rates of commission for travel agents and requiring agents to sell rail tickets for the officially listed price.
The court reiterated the CFI's logic that the railway system in Europe is essentially the joining together of national railway prices and scheduling, to create an international network.
